name: proof-vscode
description: Runs the proof CLI (proof-java, and now proof-python) and renders its verdict: inline coverage gutter, per-line test evidence, and mutation findings.

proof.jarPath.description: Path to proof-java.jar. Relative paths resolve against the workspace root. Leave empty to use the default search order (proof-java-cli/target/proof-java.jar, then .proof-java/proof-java.jar).

proof.javaExecutable.description: The Java executable used to run proof-java.jar.

proof.python.interpreter.description: The Python interpreter used to run "Proof: Analyze (Python)" - point this at the target project's own venv (e.g. .venv/Scripts/python.exe), since that is where proof-python must be installed for "-m proof_python.cli" to resolve.

proof.python.reportPath.description: Path to the coverage.py JSON report (relative to the workspace root), produced by "coverage json --show-contexts". "Proof: Analyze (Python)" reads this file - if it's missing, you get a one-time prompt with the exact commands to produce it.

proof.python.sourceRoots.description: Comma-separated source root(s), passed to proof-python's --source-roots.

proof.python.testRoots.description: Comma-separated test root(s), passed to proof-python's --test-roots.

proof.mavenExecutable.description: The Maven command used to generate a missing classpath list for Deep Scan. If left empty, "mvn.cmd" is used on Windows and "mvn" elsewhere. Set the full path if Maven isn't on PATH.

proof.gradleCoverageTask.description: The Gradle task that writes the JaCoCo XML report, used by Run Tests. Empty means "jacocoTestReport", which is the default task name of Gradle's jacoco plugin. Many builds have no task by that name: an Android module never does (AGP names coverage tasks per variant, e.g. "createDemoDebugUnitTestCoverageReport"), and a plain JVM module only has it if it applies the jacoco plugin. Run "gradlew <module>:tasks --all" to see what your build actually has. You will usually want to set proof.reportPath as well, since a non-default task writes its report somewhere Quick Scan does not look.

proof.coverageExclusions.description: Glob patterns in the style of sonar.coverage.exclusions (same syntax you'd paste into SonarQube). Passed to every analysis run as --coverage-exclusions - a single, hand-maintained list (D-05), never merged with the repo's own proof.config.json.

proof.reportPath.description: Path to the JaCoCo XML report (relative to the workspace root). "Proof: Quick Scan" reads this file - if it's missing, you get a one-time prompt to fix the setting, not a repeat warning on every run.

proof.diffMode.description: What "new code" is measured against. uncommitted (default): everything not yet committed (staged + unstaged) - i.e. what's currently sitting in your working tree. base: changes since the commit/branch named in proof.baseRef (e.g. comparing a feature branch to main). no-vcs: git is never used, "new code" can't be computed - the whole repo is shown as one coverage figure. "Proof: Deep Scan" does not run in this mode, because per-test evidence requires a diff.

proof.baseRef.description: The commit, branch, or tag to compare against when proof.diffMode is "base" (e.g. "main" or "origin/main"). Unused for other diffMode values. Setting this to HEAD itself, or to a ref that isn't an ancestor of HEAD, produces an empty diff - there's no real difference to compare.

proof.perTestClasspathPath.description: Path to the classpath list file (relative to the workspace root, one jar/output-dir per line) used by "Proof: Deep Scan". Generated automatically the first time it is needed - you do not need to create it by hand.

proof.show.explorerBadges.description: Show a coverage-percentage badge next to every file and folder in the Explorer (e.g. "85" next to Calculator.java). Independent of proof.show.lineGutter: turning this off only removes the badges, editor line colors are unaffected.

proof.show.lineGutter.description: Draw a colored line to the left of each line in an open file, showing whether it's covered (green: covered, yellow: partial, red: uncovered - a different palette applies when proof.colorblindMode is on). Independent of proof.show.explorerBadges: turning this off only removes these lines, Explorer percentage badges are unaffected.

proof.colorblindMode.description: Use a palette that stays distinguishable under all three types of color blindness (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) instead of red/green for line coverage (proof.show.lineGutter) - the Okabe-Ito palette: blue=covered, yellow=partial, vermillion=uncovered, purple="falsely green". Takes effect immediately in open editors, no window reload needed.

proof.show.oraclelessLines.description: Even when JaCoCo counts a line as covered, show it orange instead of green if NONE of the tests covering it has a real assertion (oracle) - i.e. every one of them produced a NO_RECOGNIZED_ORACLE/TAUTOLOGICAL_ORACLE/CATCH_ORACLE_WITHOUT_FAIL finding ("falsely green"). No line is ever marked this way unless per-test evidence (Proof: Deep Scan or Which Test Covers Which Line For This Class) has actually been collected - no evidence, no accusation.

proof.badgeMetric.description: Which coverage mode drives Explorer badges and line coloring. sonar-compatible (default): matches SonarQube's own percentage within +/-0.1 - it also counts branch coverage, so it usually comes out lower. jacoco-line / coverage-line: a line counts as covered if it ran at all (the highest number you'll see); these two are the same choice under the name of whichever engine produced the report - JaCoCo for Java, coverage.py for Python - and either value works with either. strict-line: a line only counts if EVERY instruction on it ran and no branch was missed (the strictest, usually the lowest). The status bar and tooltips always show all three; this setting only picks one for the badge and line color.

proof.mutationTimeout.description: Idle timeout, in seconds, for one module in mutation testing (--mutation-timeout): the run is stopped once no class has completed for this long - not a total budget, so a run that keeps completing classes keeps going however long it takes. When it does trigger, the result is partial and still shown, never silently dropped. Single-class runs are usually seconds long; you may need to raise this if one class legitimately needs longer than the default between completions.

proof.perTestTimeout.description: Time budget, in seconds, for one module in Deep Scan (--per-test-timeout). If exceeded, the run stops (PER_TEST_COLLECTION_FAILED). The default is usually enough for a handful of classes changed in a diff; you may need to raise it for a run that targets many classes at once, such as "Deep Scan Whole Module Anyway".

proof.testCommandPhase.description: Which Maven phase "Proof: Run Tests" runs. test (default): the shortest path, usually enough to produce the JaCoCo report. verify: needed if your modules require a packaged jar (e.g. a JPMS/OSGi test) - takes longer.

proof.jacocoPluginVersion.description: The org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin version "Proof: Run Tests" binds from the command line when the pom doesn't declare the JaCoCo plugin at all. Unused if the pom already declares its own JaCoCo version - the pom itself is never touched.

kind.description: The kind of task proof-java itself launches (e.g. runTests).

commands.title: Proof: Install Skill for AI Agent
Proof: Which Test Covers Which Line For This Class
Proof: Deep Scan Whole Module (no diff)
Proof: Mutation Testing - Whole Module (no diff)

view/item/context.when: view == proof.qualityView || view == proof.coverageView || view == proof.lineTestsView || view == proof.mutationView

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:integration
